biography: Rasmus Lindh, a name increasingly whispered in racing circles, hails from Gothenburg, Sweden. Unlike many who practically grow up in karting, Rasmus's path was ignited by a chance visit to a local racing event at age 14. Captivated by the roar of the engines and the electric atmosphere, he badgered his parents until they relented and enrolled him in a karting school. While other kids were playing video games, Rasmus was mastering the art of apexes and braking points on icy Swedish tracks. His raw talent quickly became apparent, and within a few years, he was competing in Formula racing, earning podiums and turning heads. Now, at 26, Rasmus is making waves in the IMSA series, piloting the Oreca 07 #81. While still proving himself on the global stage, his flamboyant style and undeniable speed suggest a bright future lies ahead. He's no longer just a promising talent; he's a driver to watch, hungry for victory and eager to etch his name into racing history. The pressure is on, but Rasmus seems to thrive under it, much like the Swedish winter, he's cold and calculating.
drivingStyle: Rasmus Lindh is known for his aggressive, attacking driving style. He is a late-braking specialist, often throwing the car into corners with incredible precision and daring. While this sometimes results in spectacular overtakes, it can also lead to oversteering and tire degradation. He tends to be less conservative with tire management than some of his rivals, preferring to push hard from the start and adapt his strategy as needed. In high-pressure situations, Rasmus tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes to his detriment. He relishes wheel-to-wheel combat and isn't afraid to make bold moves, even if it means taking risks.

rivalries.reason: A clash on the track during a Formula 3 race resulted in both drivers retiring. The incident was deemed a racing incident, but the bad blood between them remains.

Dubois and Lindh battled fiercely for the championship in a junior series, with Dubois ultimately winning by a narrow margin. Lindh feels he was robbed of the title and is determined to prove himself superior.

Tanaka, a seasoned veteran, has publicly criticized Lindh's aggressive driving style, calling him reckless. Lindh dismisses Tanaka as being 'past his prime' and is eager to prove his speed against the older driver.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of blue socks, even when they are full of holes.
Listens to Swedish death metal at full volume for at least 30 minutes before every race.
Has a habit of talking to his car, giving it pep talks and occasionally scolding it.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Indy Pro 2000 Championship in 2019. He dominated the season, showcasing his talent and securing his place as a rising star in open-wheel racing.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of a Formula Regional Americas race in 2020. The incident cost him the championship and severely dented his confidence.
